content: The buccal testosterone system and pretomanid can increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms not fully understood. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative medications. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, and patients should avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs, except for bedaquiline and linezolid. Similarly, intranasal testosterone and pretomanid, as well as topical testosterone and pretomanid, can increase each other's toxicity. These combinations should also be avoided or replaced with alternative treatments. The same caution applies to thioguanine, ticlopidine, valproic acid, vitamin A, and vitamin D when used with pretomanid. In all cases, the risk of hepatotoxicity necessitates avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents. Pretomanid can increase the levels or effects of valsartan, verapamil, voxilaprevir, and zidovudine. Close monitoring is required when co-administering pretomanid with these drugs, particularly those that are sensitive substrates of OATP1B3, P-gp, or OAT3 transporters. Increased monitoring for adverse effects is advised, and dosage adjustments may be necessary. The use of pretomanid in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid has been associated with several adverse effects, including peripheral neuropathy (81%), acne (39%), anemia (37%), nausea (37%), vomiting (34%), musculoskeletal pain (29%), headache (28%), increased transaminases (28%), dyspepsia (24%), decreased appetite (22%), rash (21%), pruritus (20%), abdominal pain (19%), pleuritic pain (19%), increased GGT (17%), lower respiratory tract infections (15%), hyperamylasemia (14%), hemoptysis (13%), cough (12%), visual impairment (12%), hypoglycemia (11%), abnormal weight loss (10%), diarrhea (10%), constipation (8%), gastritis (8%), neutropenia (8%), dry skin (7%), hypertension (7%), prolonged QT on ECG (6%), hyperlipasemia (6%), insomnia (6%), and thrombocytopenia (6%). Pretomanid is contraindicated in patients for whom bedaquiline or linezolid is contraindicated. Hepatic adverse reactions have been reported with this combination, and treatment interruption may be necessary. Liver function tests, including ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin, should be obtained at baseline, at two weeks, and then monthly. Myelosuppression, a known adverse effect of linezolid, has also been reported, and linezolid dosing may need to be reduced or interrupted if myelosuppression worsens. Peripheral and optic neuropathy, also associated with linezolid, may require discontinuation of linezolid. QT prolongation has been reported with the combination, although pretomanid alone has not demonstrated QTc prolongation in cardiac electrophysiology testing. Discontinue treatment if significant ventricular arrhythmia or a QTcF interval greater than 500 ms develops. If syncope occurs, obtain an ECG to check for QT prolongation. Pretomanid has been shown to cause testicular atrophy and impaired fertility in male rats, but its effects on human male fertility have not been fully evaluated. Lactic acidosis, a known adverse effect of linezolid, has been reported with the combination. Patients experiencing recurrent nausea or vomiting should be evaluated immediately, including checking bicarbonate and lactic acid levels. Linezolid dosing or the entire combination may need to be interrupted. There is no data on the use of pretomanid in pregnant women or its presence in human milk. However, it has been detected in rat milk, suggesting it may also be present in human milk. Due to the potential for adverse reactions in nursing infants, the benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for the drug and potential risks to the infant. Pretomanid is metabolized by multiple reductive and oxidative pathways, with no single pathway being dominant. CYP3A4 is responsible for approximately 20% of its metabolism. The drug should be taken with food, and the tablet should be swallowed whole with water. Pretomanid must only be used in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid as part of the recommended dosing regimen. Emphasize the importance of compliance with the full course of therapy to patients, and administer the combination regimen under directly observed therapy. Store the medication at room temperature, below 86°F (30°C). This information is provided for general educational purposes. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Always consult the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
